{{Short description|British dairy products company}} {{Use dmy dates|date=January 2020}} {{Infobox company | name = Saputo Dairy UK | logo = Saputo Dairy UK logo.png | logo_size = | type = Limited Company | former_name = Dairy Crest plc | founded = 1981 | hq_location = [[Weybridge]], [[Surrey]], [[United Kingdom]] | key_people = Steve Douglas
(COO) | industry = [[Dairy product|Dairy Products]] | products = Cathedral City (cheese)
Clover
Petits Filous | revenue = £456.8 million (2018){{cite web|url=https://www.dairycrest.co.uk/media/1077/annual-report-2018.pdf|title=Annual Report 2018|publisher=Dairy Crest|access-date=17 March 2019}}{{Dead link|date=January 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} | operating_income = £71.4 million (2018){{needs update|date=December 2025}} | net_income = £149.5 million (2018){{needs update|date=December 2025}} | num_employees = 1,097 (2018){{needs update|date=December 2025}} | subsidiaries = | owner = [[Saputo Inc.]] | website = {{URL|http://uk.saputo.com/}} }} '''Saputo Dairy UK''', also Dairy Crest Limited, is a British dairy products company. It was created in 2019 when the Canadian company [[Saputo Inc.|Saputo Inc]] bought the Dairy Crest company, which had been created in 1981 as a spin-off of the [[Milk Marketing Board]].{{Cite web|title=Dairy Crest becomes Saputo Dairy UK|url=https://www.dairyreporter.com/Article/2019/07/03/Dairy-Crest-becomes-Saputo-Dairy-UK|access-date=7 July 2020|website=dairyreporter.com|date=3 July 2019 |language=en-GB}}{{Cite web|title=SAPUTO DAIRY UK LTD - Filing history (free information from Companies House)|url=https://beta.companieshouse.gov.uk/company/11834952/filing-history|access-date=7 July 2020|website=beta.companieshouse.gov.uk|language=en}} Its brands include [[Cathedral City Cheddar]] cheese, Country Life butter, Utterly Butterly, [[Vitalite]], [[Wensleydale Creamery|Wensleydale]] and [[Clover (spread)|Clover]]. Dairy Crest processed and sold milk (wholesale and via doorstep deliveries) and owned the milkshake brand [[Frijj]] until the sale of that part of the business to Germany's [[Müller (company)|Müller]] in 2015. The company was listed on the [[London Stock Exchange]] as Dairy Crest plc, until it was acquired by Saputo in 2019.{{cite news |url=https://www.thegrocer.co.uk/dairy/dairy-crest-name-to-disappear-as-it-rebrands-to-saputo-dairy-uk/593370.article|title=Dairy Crest name to disappear as it rebrands to Saputo Dairy UK|newspaper=www.thegrocer.co.uk|date=15 May 2019|access-date=14 August 2020}} Saputo rebranded the company under its own name later that year. ==History== Dairy Crest was established in 1981 as the milk processing arm of the [[Milk Marketing Board]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.dairycrest.co.uk/ourbusiness/ourhistory.asp |title=Dairly Crest History |access-date=25 August 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080918091122/http://www.dairycrest.co.uk/ourbusiness/ourhistory.asp|archive-date=18 September 2008|url-status=dead }} In 1983, the company launched Clover, a dairy spread. The company established a joint venture with French dairy company [[Yoplait]] in 1981, called Yoplait Dairy Crest. YDC is 51% owned by Yoplait and 49% by Dairy Crest, and distributes Yoplait brand products in the UK. In 1995, Dairy Crest bought the Cathedral City brand of cheese from Mendip Foods Ltd. The business was [[privatised]] the following year and Dairy Crest was listed on the [[London Stock Exchange]]. [[File:Dairy Crest Logo.svg|thumb|150px|Logo of Dairy Crest]] In 2000, Dairy Crest acquired the dairy and cheese products division of [[Unigate]] in London, and in 2002 bought the [[St Ivel]] spreads company, which had been based in [[Wootton Bassett]] in [[Wiltshire]]. It acquired the Country Life butter brand from the English Butter Marketing Company in 2004, and [[Express Dairies]] from [[Arla Foods]] in 2006 for £33 million.{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2006/jul/24/food.money|title=Dairy Crest buys rival to expand milk round|author=Mark Tran|work=[[The Guardian]]|date=24 July 2006|access-date=26 March 2015}} The company sold the majority of its own-label cheese business to its Scottish equivalent [[First Milk (company)|First Milk]] in 2006, along with the creameries and factory that produced most of the products concerned.{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/business/5380606.stm|title=Dairy Crest sells cheese business|work=BBC News|date=26 September 2006|access-date=26 March 2015}} In 2007, Dairy Crest bought St Hubert for £248 million, securing the Cholegram, Le Fleurier, Omega 3 and Vallé brands, which were subsequently sold in 2012 to [[Montagu Private Equity]] for €430 million (£347 million).{{cite web|url=https://www.ft.com/content/693db296-c1fc-11e1-8e7c-00144feabdc0|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220710134419/https://www.ft.com/content/693db296-c1fc-11e1-8e7c-00144feabdc0|archive-date=10 July 2022|url-access=subscription|title=Dairy Crest sells St Hubert|work=www.ft.com|date=29 June 2012|access-date=10 July 2022|url-status=bot: unknown}} Plans for the [[Crudgington]] Creamery to close were announced in 2012.{{cite news |url=https://farming.co.uk/news/dairy-crest-to-close-shropshire-creamery|title=Dairy Crest to close Shropshire creamery|newspaper=farming.co.uk|date=21 September 2012|access-date=14 August 2020}} The creamery closed in May 2014, when production of spreads was concentrated at [[Kirkby]] on Merseyside while the research and development facility was transferred to an innovation centre built by the company at [[Harper Adams University]], Shropshire{{cite news |author=Emma Walker |date=12 June 2015 |title=Demolition to start at creamery, Landmark buildings to disappear |work=Shropshire Star |page=6}} ===Sale of milk business=== [[Image:Dairy Crest Milk Float Garage 2.jpg|thumb|right|A Dairy Crest [[Smith Electric Vehicles|Smith's]] Elizabethan milk float in 2008]] Dairy Crest sold its doorstep milk delivery operations in the [[North West England|North West of England]] in July 2013 to Creamline Dairies who now operate the milk rounds from the depots in [[Warrington]], [[Flixton, Greater Manchester|Flixton]], [[Stockport]] and [[Macclesfield]], while Mortons operate rounds in [[Metropolitan Borough of Wirral|Wirral]], [[Chester]] and [[Liverpool]].{{cite web|url=http://www.creamline.co.uk/dairy-crest-customers|title=Creamline FAQs - General FAQs - Help and Support|work=creamline.co.uk|access-date=26 March 2015|archive-date=16 March 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140316224940/http://www.creamline.co.uk/dairy-crest-customers|url-status=dead}} Dairy Crest announced a drop in profits on 6 November 2014, down 95% to £900,000 in the six months to September.{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-29929561|title=Dairy Crest sells milk operations as profits slump|publisher=BBC News|date=6 November 2014|access-date=6 November 2014}} The company agreed the sale of its entire legacy milk business, which processes and distributes milk, as well as the [[Frijj]] milkshake brand, to Germany's [[Müller (company)|Müller]] for £80 million, enabling it to be combined with Müller's existing subsidiary, [[Müller Wiseman Dairies]]. The sale was approved by the [[Competition and Markets Authority]] on 19 October 2015,{{cite news|last1=Ratcliffe|first1=Madeline|title=Dairy Crest share price rises as CMA approves Muller takeover|url=http://www.cityam.com/226853/dairy-crest-share-price-rises-as-cma-approves-muller-takeover|access-date=23 October 2015|work=City AM|date=19 October 2015}} and completed the following December.{{cite news|last1=Daneshkhu|first1=Scheherazade|title=Dairy Crest loses taste for UK milk production with Müller deal|url=http://www.ft.com/cms/s/0/e1bc9750-aa56-11e5-955c-1e1d6de94879.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151230232703/http://www.ft.com/cms/s/0/e1bc9750-aa56-11e5-955c-1e1d6de94879.html#axzz3vePpyZ4I|archive-date=30 December 2015|url-access=subscription|url-status=bot: unknown|access-date=28 December 2015|work=Financial Times|date=28 December 2015}} ===Acquisition by Saputo=== It was announced in 2019 that Canadian dairy company [[Saputo Inc.|Saputo Inc]] would be buying Dairy Crest.{{cite news |title=Cathedral City firm to be bought for £975m |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-47329330 |access-date=22 February 2019 |work=BBC News |date=22 February 2019}} The company was valued at £975 million, making each share worth 620p.{{cite news |last1=Onita |first1=Laura |title=Dairy Crest deal set to net boss Mark Allen £4.8 million |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/business/dairy-crest-deal-set-to-net-boss-mark-allen-48-million-a4073956.html |access-date=22 February 2019 |work=Evening Standard |date=22 February 2019 |language=en}} The transaction was completed on 15 April 2019.{{cite web|url=https://www.foodmanufacture.co.uk/Article/2019/04/18/Dairy-processor-completes-Dairy-Crest-purchase|title=Saputo completes acquisition of Dairy Crest|date=18 April 2019|publisher=Food Manufacture|access-date=19 April 2019}} At the time of the sale, Dairy Crest was the fourth largest dairy company in the UK based on turnover.{{Cite web|last=White|first=Kevin|title=Who owns the dairy industry? The 10 biggest dairy companies in the UK|url=https://www.thegrocer.co.uk/rankings/who-owns-the-dairy-industry-the-10-biggest-dairy-companies-in-the-uk/590833.article|access-date=2020-07-07|website=The Grocer|language=en}} Saputo renamed the business under its own brand in July 2019, though Dairy Crest Limited remained the principal legal entity.{{cite news |last1=Sandercock |first1=Henry |title=Dairy Crest brand replaced by new owner Saputo |url=https://www.thegrocer.co.uk/dairy/dairy-crest-brand-replaced-by-new-owner-saputo/595116.article |access-date=12 April 2020 |work=The Grocer |date=4 July 2019}} In 2021, Saputo purchased Bute Island Foods, the manufacturer of Sheese vegan cheese.{{cite news |title=Vegan cheesemaker sold in multi-million pound deal |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-scotland-business-57383638 |access-date=8 December 2025 |work=BBC News |date=7 June 2021}} The company supplies cheese, spreads and drinks. Cheese brands include [[Cathedral City Cheddar|Cathedral City]], [[Davidstow Cheddar]] and Wexford.{{Cite web |title=Dairy Crest: Brands |url=http://www.dairycrest.co.uk/our-brands--products.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100312060039/http://www.dairycrest.co.uk/our-brands--products.aspx |archive-date=12 March 2010 |access-date=20 March 2010}} Spread brands include [[Clover (spread)|Clover]], Country Life, Utterly Butterly, [[Vitalite]] and Willow. Spread and Frylight cooking spray production is consolidated at [[Kirkby]].{{Cite web |title=Dairy Crest: Locations |url=http://www.dairycrest.co.uk/our-business/our-locations.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100327212721/http://www.dairycrest.co.uk/our-business/our-locations.aspx |archive-date=27 March 2010 |access-date=20 March 2010}} [[Davidstow Creamery]] in Cornwall has been run by the company since 1981. ==Pollution== At [[Truro Crown Court]] in December 2021, Dairy Crest admitted charges relating to a series of incidents of serious pollution between December 2015 and January 2021, including the illegal discharge of "biological sludge" and "suspended solids" from its creamery at [[Davidstow]] into the [[River Inny, Cornwall|River Inny]], Cornwall.{{cite news|title=Discharge from Davidstow Cathedral City cheese factory poisoned fish|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-cornwall-59597830 |work=BBC News|date=10 December 2021|accessdate=13 December 2021}} Fines of £1.52 million and costs of £272,747 were imposed on the company in June 2022.{{cite news|title=Davidstow Cathedral City cheese firm pollution fine|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-cornwall-61914566|work=BBC News|date=23 June 2022|accessdate=23 June 2022}} It was reported that there was a possibility that the company's [[Royal warrant of appointment (United Kingdom)|royal warrant]] could be removed as a result of the pollution.{{Cite news |last=Horton |first=Helena |last2=reporter |first2=Helena Horton Environment |date=2022-06-29 |title=Queen could revoke Davidstow cheddar royal warrant over river pollution |url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2022/jun/29/queen-could-revoke-davidstow-cheddar-dairy-crest-royal-warrant-river-pollution |access-date=2026-02-10 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}} Pollution in 2023 and 2025 in a tributary of the [[River Ure]] was caused by a faulty drainage system at its Wensleydale Creamery in [[Hawes]], North Yorkshire.{{Cite news |title=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ckg1pz2kxkpo}} In 2025 the company said it was making the switch from producing demineralised whey and galacto-oligosaccharides, which it began producing in 2013, in order to return to the production of sweet whey powder.{{Cite news |title=Cornwall's Davidstow Creamery to lose 60 jobs amid Saputo Dairy cuts |url=https://www.thepost.uk.com/news/cornwalls-davidstow-creamery-to-lose-60-jobs-amid-saputo-dairy-cuts-780443}} The Environment Agency cited the Davidstow site as a persistently poorly performing site in the 2024–25 Chief Regulator’s report.{{Cite web |title=Environment Agency Chief Regulator’s report 2024-25 |url=https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/environment-agency-chief-regulators-report-2024-25/environment-agency-chief-regulators-report-2024-25}} In 2026, the Environment Agency initiated a consultation process for a new permit at the Davidstow creamery, which aims to introduce environmental improvements and allow an increase in cheese production.{{Cite web |date=19 January 2026 |title=Environment Agency Proposes New Permit for Saputo Dairy UK to Enhance Production |url=https://dairynews.today/news/environment-agency-proposes-new-permit-for-saputo-dairy-uk-to-enhance-production.html |access-date=2026-07-13 |website=dairynews.today |language=en}} ==References==
